items.title: Not Failing to See Directly: When a Working Sense Faculty Actually Counts

items.zh: 非不現見現量者，復有四種。謂諸根不壞，作意現前，相似生故；超越生故；無障礙故；非極遠故。
items.en: Not failing to see directly, as a condition of direct perception, again has four aspects: that the faculties are unimpaired and attention is present, because of matched arising; because of transcending arising; because there is no obstruction; and because it is not excessively distant.

items.zh: 相似生者，謂欲界諸根於欲界境，上地諸根於上地境，已生已等生，若生若起，是名相似生。超越生者，謂上地諸根於下地境，已生等如前說，是名超越生。
items.en: Matched arising: it means desire-realm faculties meeting desire-realm objects, and higher-realm faculties meeting higher-realm objects... this is called matched arising. Transcending arising: it means higher-realm faculties meeting lower-realm objects, arising as explained above; this is called transcending arising.

items.zh: 無障礙者，復有四種。一、非覆障所礙，二、非隱障所礙，三、非映障所礙，四、非惑障所礙。覆障所礙者，謂黑闇、無明闇、不澄清色闇所覆障。隱障所礙者，謂或藥草力、或呪術力、或神通力之所隱障。映障所礙者，謂少小物為廣多物之所映奪，故不可得。如飲食中藥，或復毛端。如是等類無量無邊。且如小光，大光所映，故不可得。所謂日光映星月等。又如月光映奪眾星。又如能治映奪所治，令不可得。謂不淨作意映奪淨相，無常、苦、無我、作意映奪常、樂、我相，無相作意映奪一切眾相。惑障所礙者，謂幻化所作，或色相殊勝，或復相似；或內所作，目眩、惛、夢、悶、醉、放逸，或復顛狂。如是等類名為惑障。若不為此四障所礙，名無障礙。
items.en: Free of obstruction again has four aspects: first, not hindered by a covering obstruction; second, not hindered by a concealing obstruction; third, not hindered by an eclipsing obstruction; and fourth, not hindered by a deluding obstruction... where none of these four kinds of obstruction applies, this is called freedom from obstruction.

items.zh: 非極遠者，謂非三種極遠所遠。一、處極遠，二、時極遠，三、損減極遠。如是一切，總名非不現見。非不現故，名為現量。
items.en: Not excessively distant means being distant in none of three ways: first, excessive distance of place; second, excessive distance of time; and third, excessive distance through diminution... All of this together is called not failing to see directly. Because it does not fail to see directly, it is called direct perception.

items.title: Not Already Deliberated Nor Yet to Be Deliberated: The Instant Before Thought

items.zh: 非已思應思現量者，復有二種。一、纔取便成取所依境，二、建立境界取所依境。
items.en: Not a matter already deliberated on or yet to be deliberated on, as a condition of direct perception, again has two aspects: first, an object that, the very instant it is grasped, already serves as the basis of that grasping; and second, an object that serves as the basis of the grasping that establishes an [inner] object.

items.zh: 纔取便成取所依境者，謂若境能作纔取便成取所依止。
猶如良醫授病者藥，色、香、味、觸皆悉圓滿，有大勢力，成熟威德。當知此藥色、香、味觸纔取便成取所依止。藥之所有大勢威德，病若未愈，名為應思；其病若愈，名為已思。
items.en: It is like a skilled physician giving medicine to a patient — its colour, smell, taste, and texture all complete, possessed of great potency, accomplished in efficacy. Know that this medicine's colour, smell, taste, and texture, the very instant they are taken, already serve as the basis of that taking. But the medicine's great potency and efficacy — if the illness is not yet cured, this is called "yet to be deliberated"; if the illness is cured, this is called "already deliberated."

items.zh: 如是等類，名纔取便成取所依境。建立境界取所依境者，謂若境能為建立境界取所依止。
如瑜伽師，於地思惟水、火、風界。若住於地思惟其水，即住地想轉作水想。若住於地思惟火、風，即住地想轉作火、風想。此中地想、即是建立境界之取。地者，即是建立境界取之所依。
items.en: It is like a yogic practitioner who, from the earth-element, contemplates the water, fire, and wind elements. Abiding in the earth and contemplating its water, the perception of earth turns into the perception of water; abiding in the earth and contemplating its fire or wind, the perception of earth turns into the perception of fire or wind... Here, the perception of earth is precisely the grasping that establishes the object; the earth itself is precisely the basis of that grasping.

items.zh: 如住於地，住水、火、風、如其所應，當知亦爾。是名建立境界取所依境。此中建立境界取所依境，非已思惟，非應思惟。地等諸界，解若未成、名應思惟；解若成就，名已思惟。如是名為非已思應思現量。

items.title: Direct Perception Complete: Seven Errors to Avoid, Four Kinds Confirmed

items.zh: 非錯亂境界現量者，謂或五種、或七種。五種者，謂非五種錯亂境界。何等為五？一、想錯亂，二、數錯亂，三、形錯亂，四、顯錯亂，五、業錯亂。七種者，謂非七種錯亂境界。何等為七？謂即前五，及餘二種遍行錯亂，合為七種。何等為二？一、心錯亂，二、見錯亂。
items.en: Not a deceptive object, as a condition of direct perception, means being free of either five or seven kinds of deception. The five: what are they? First, deception of perception; second, deception of number; third, deception of shape; fourth, deception of colour; and fifth, deception of function. The seven: these are the same five, together with two further deceptions that pervade all the rest, making seven in all. What are the two? First, deception of mind; and second, deception of view.

items.zh: 想錯亂者，謂於非彼相，起彼相想。如於陽焰、鹿渴相中，起於水想。數錯亂者，謂於少數起多數增上慢。如瞖眩者，於一月處見多月像。形錯亂者，謂於餘形色起餘形色增上慢。如於旋火見彼輪形。顯錯亂者，謂於餘顯色起餘顯色增上慢。如迦末羅病損壞眼根，於非黃色悉見黃相。業錯亂者，謂於無業事起有業增上慢。如結拳馳走，見樹奔流。
items.en: Deception of perception: taking up the perception of one thing where that thing is not present — as when a mirage, mistaken by thirsty deer, gives rise to the perception of water. Deception of number: an inflated conviction of many where there are few — as one with clouded, dazzled eyes sees many moons where there is one. Deception of function: an inflated conviction of activity where there is none — as one running with a clenched fist sees the trees themselves rushing past.

items.zh: 心錯亂者，謂即於五種所錯亂義，心生喜樂。見錯亂者，謂即於五種所錯亂義，忍受、顯說、生吉祥想，堅執不捨。若非如是錯亂境界，名為現量。
items.en: Deception of mind: taking delight in these same five deceptions. Deception of view: accepting these same five deceptions, proclaiming them, regarding them as auspicious, and holding to them firmly without letting go. Where the object is free of deception of this kind, it is called direct perception.

items.zh: 問：如是現量，誰所有耶？答：略說四種所有。一、色根現量，二、意受現量，三、世間現量，四、清淨現量。色根現量者，謂五色根所行境界，如先所說現量體相。意受現量者，謂諸意根所行境界，如先所說現量體相。世間現量者，謂即二種，總說為一世間現量。清淨現量者，謂諸所有世間現量，亦得名為清淨現量。或有清淨現量，非世間現量。謂出世智，於所行境，有知為有，無知為無，有上知有上，無上知無上。如是等類，名不共世間清淨現量。
items.en: Question: to whom, then, does direct perception of this kind belong? Answer: briefly, it belongs to four kinds of possessors. First, direct perception of the physical faculties; second, direct perception received by the mind; third, worldly direct perception; and fourth, pure direct perception. Worldly direct perception is these first two kinds together, spoken of as one. Pure direct perception refers to all worldly direct perception, which may equally be called pure direct perception — but there is also a pure direct perception that is not worldly direct perception: namely, transcendent wisdom which, regarding its object, knows what has being as having being and what has no being as having none, knows what is surpassable as surpassable and what is unsurpassed as unsurpassed. Direct perception of this kind is called pure direct perception not shared with the world.

blocks.text: Today's reading is a careful account of **perception** (現量, *pratyakṣa*), the first means of valid knowledge. For a Yogācāra reader it is important: it defines what counts as direct experience, as opposed to inference, memory, or imagination. The examples come from ordinary life and from meditation.

Perception is valid when its object is **not unseen**, **not already deliberated nor yet to be deliberated**, and **not deceptive**. Venerable Miào Jìng: 量 means a standard (what fits it is right) and knowing.

A working faculty must actually meet the object. An object may be unseen because it is obstructed (by one of three "darknesses", which Venerable Miào Jìng ranks: murky matter, which still has some light; ignorance, heavier; and pitch darkness), too far, too subtle, or of a different realm. Master Cháng Bǎi: higher faculties can take lower objects, but lower faculties cannot take higher ones. "Excessive distance through diminution" is, Venerable Miào Jìng explains, analysing matter in meditation down to particles too fine to perceive (Day 16).

Perception is the moment before thought: neither the thought that has already formed nor the one about to form. In a meditation on the earth element, Venerable Miào Jìng says, "abiding in the earth-perception is direct perception; thinking of water while water hasn't appeared is not." The *Pīxún jì* adds that both the formed and the forming understanding are conceptual, not perception.
Master Cháng Bǎi uses the treatise's example of a physician's medicine: its colour and smell are perceived; its "great potency and efficacy" can only be inferred, by observing whether it works.

Perception must be free of seven errors: of perception, number, shape, colour, activity, mind, and view. Master Cháng Bǎi: a magician pulling a rabbit from a handkerchief presents a deceptive object; no rabbit is there. Some errors involve "inflated conviction", which Venerable Miào Jìng characterises: "inwardly sincere, not deceiving anyone; one truly believes it is so, but is mistaken" (Day 66's overestimator).

Perception is of four kinds: by the material faculties (the five senses), by the mind, worldly, and pure. All worldly perception "may also be called pure", Venerable Miào Jìng explains, when it is wholesome or neutral.

The definition prepares a central question. If perception is the moment before conceptualisation, then what we usually call "seeing a table" is already mostly inference and naming (Days 2, 18). Yogācāra will argue that even the bare moment presents only what consciousness presents. This passage gives the epistemological tools for that argument.

quiz.q: What two meanings of 量 does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: first, a standard — what fits it is right; second, knowing — mind has the function of knowing
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "What fits this standard is right, what doesn't is wrong — so 量 has the sense of a standard." Its second sense is knowing: mental phenomena have the function of knowing.

quiz.q: What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give of an object that fails "not being deceptive"?
options: a magician producing a rabbit from a handkerchief — deceptive, illusory, not perception, for no rabbit is there
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a magician pulling a rabbit from a handkerchief is deceptive and illusory; it cannot be called direct perception, because there is no rabbit there. He also adds Dignāga's four kinds of perception.

quiz.q: "Transcending arising" is higher-realm faculties meeting lower objects. Can it work the other way, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: higher faculties can take lower objects; lower faculties cannot take higher ones — hard, unless one attains form-realm concentration
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Higher faculties can take lower objects; lower faculties cannot take higher objects — that is very hard, unless one attains form-realm concentration." Venerable Miào Jìng: then the faculties carry form-realm elements — the divine eye and ear.

quiz.q: The covering obstruction has three darknesses. How does Venerable Miào Jìng rank them?
options: the murky-matter darkness still has some light — lightest; the ignorance-darkness heavier; pitch darkness heaviest
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the darkness of unclear matter still has some light; the darkness of ignorance is heavier; pitch darkness heavier still. f15 omits the definitions of all four obstructions, which the lectures explain.

quiz.q: In the physician's medicine analogy, what is the medicine's "great potency and efficacy," per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: known only by inference — one must observe and reflect whether it works
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The medicine's great potency is known only by inference — one must still observe and reflect whether it is effective." Its colour, smell, taste, and touch are grasped instantly; its efficacy is deliberated.

quiz.q: A yogin abiding in the earth-perception contemplates water. When, per Venerable Miào Jìng, is it perception and when not?
options: abiding in earth-perception is perception; imagining water before it appears is not, since the object isn't present
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Abiding in the earth-perception, this is direct perception; thinking of water while water hasn't appeared, that is not, because the object isn't present." The note's "transferring" perception contradicts this.

quiz.q: The definitions of deception use 增上慢, "inflated conviction." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say it means here?
options: inwardly sincerely believing it so — not deceiving anyone — yet mistaken
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Inwardly it is sincere — not deceiving anyone; one truly believes it is so, but is mistaken; hence 'inflated conviction.'" f15 omits the definitions of shape- and colour-deception.
